reason: The contract requires exact (zero-tolerance) CRC-32/ISO-HDLC equality with zlib.crc32 for every legal uint8 [B,N] input (B in [1,128], N in {64,128}). All three in-scope failure hypotheses were rebutted with decisive runtime evidence: c1 — the host-computed composition factors and correction term exactly match a directly iterated bit-advance for all chunks at widths 64/128 (including the 0x80000000 identity) and host emulation matches zlib exactly; c2 — run() output exactly equals zlib.crc32 on 1904 rows covering both widths, edge batches B=1/7/128, all-zero, all-0xFF, random (two seeds), single-byte patterns, and contiguous views, with int64 output and only benign deprecation warnings (not a contract violation in the frozen Triton 3.4.0 environment); c3 — is_neg()/is_conj() exist on torch 2.8.0 and run() returns a fresh int64 tensor without exception. The evidence covers the risk map's remaining surfaces (uint32 semantics, tl.reduce, indexing, output dtype). No open claims remain, and the Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence and found no new claims. Since CRC is a linear map over GF(2) and the composition coefficients were verified bit-exact for every chunk, exact equality on structured and random rows plus verified coefficients provides strong, essentially exhaustive-per-structure assurance across the full byte domain.
